analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 10.15.26
key_insights: Tech/AI sell-off extended overnight: futures indicated lower (NDX -115bps / SPX -25bps). Korea finished -7% (Samsung -10%, Hynix -11%), Nikkei -5%, HK Tech -3%.

GS PB: Global Fundamental LS managers were down 0.8% (-1.7 StdDev) on the prior day, mainly beta. TMT-focused funds were down 2.7% (-2.6 StdDev). The SPX ex-AI index (SPXXAI) finished +60bps, a top 5 move vs SPX YTD.
AI complex concerns center on credit, capital and competition. Optical, Semicap and Hardware are indicated lower, while IT Services and Telcos are indicated higher.

TSM is -2% after a solid quarter. FY26 revenue growth was raised to ~44% YoY (from 40%), but 3Q GM of 66.4% was down 1.3ppts QoQ and a touch light. The desk will watch price action given the ASML reaction the day before.

TSM 4Q26 revenue is guided up 14% QoQ at the midpoint (vs BBGe +10%), with GM of 65-67%. Management sees no signs of AI demand slowing, with Agentic AI driving incremental CPU and networking demand. This could push the AI accelerator CAGR above the previously guided high-50%, excluding CPUs.

TSM FY26 CapEx was reiterated at US$60-64bn. Management said it is too early to comment on FY27 CapEx but that FY26-28 spending will be significantly above prior years. N2 capacity is expected to more than double in 2027, with aggressive N3 expansion across Taiwan, Arizona and Japan. Overseas fabs dilute FY26 GM by ~2ppts, widening to 3-4ppts later in the five-year plan.

Global memory complex is indicated lower (SKHY -7%, WDC/STX/SNDK -5%). Local desk notes foreigners have sold Hynix for 15 straight sessions and Samsung for 5. Elon Musk drew attention to China memory production on X ('China will be making a LOT of RAM in 2028').
Bloomberg reports ByteDance is in advanced talks to buy bespoke AI ASICs from MediaTek for data centers. ByteDance would become MediaTek's second major ASIC customer after Google.

IDC: global smartphone shipments fell 22.0% YoY to 255.3 million units in 3Q26, the largest YoY decline of any quarter on record, as the AI-led memory crisis raises component costs and strains supply. Apple and Samsung gain share.

The 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals unanimously allowed Florida to enforce H.B. 3, barring children under 14 from social media, and vacated the lower court's preliminary injunction on First Amendment grounds.

SPOT Q3'26 preview (Sheridan): 3Q revenue estimate of EUR4.964bn is modestly below company guidance of EUR5.0bn and slightly below consensus. Premium subscribers of 305mn and MAUs of 788mn are aligned with targets. GS lowers 2026 estimates on lower 2H advertising revenue and FX.

Macro pre-market: E-minis -35bps, Nasdaq futures -1.3%, 10-year yield lower at 5.08% on growth concerns, Brent -1.6%. Pre-market SMH -2.5%, DRAM -6%, CRWV -5%. Europe is mixed (FTSE +50bps, CAC +10bps, DAX -50bps), with telecom and staples outperforming and tech lagging.
Reports that the US may ease Russian shadow-fleet sanctions, while Ukraine resumed attacks on Russian refineries.
Data and speakers today: PPI, Initial Jobless Claims, Retail Sales, Philly Fed and Empire State Manufacturing at 8:30am. Fed Pres Goolsbee at 10am, Hammack at 4:30pm, Fed Chairman Warsh at 11:30pm.

SEMICON West takeaways: GS remains bullish on semiconductors, with an incrementally positive view on WFE growth for 2027 and 2028, consistent with its recent WFE outlook. Meetings included Applied Materials, Lam Research, Teradyne, Camtek, Onto Innovation and MKS Instruments.

Accenture Investor Day: multi-year guidance is mid-single digit revenue growth in FY27-28, mid-to-high single digit in FY29, and 10-30bps annual operating margin expansion. GS expects it to mute the bear case and stays Buy. A further re-rating needs several quarters of organic revenue acceleration plus gross margin expansion.

Dynatrace F2Q preview: GS reiterates Buy and raises PT to $71. Visible Alpha consensus CC NNARR is ~$74M (+5% YoY). GS sees ~$4-5M of upside as a baseline (vs ~$7M organic in F1Q). A raise to the organic F2H outlook would carry more weight, as it would signal confidence in DPS cohort renewals.

MongoDB: Chief Product Officer for AI and Emerging Products Pablo Stern and Chief Customer Officer Erica Volini are leaving after Dev Ittycheria returned as interim CEO. The company says there is no strategy change. GS says the leadership transition adds uncertainty while the CEO search continues.

Music in the Air 10-year update: the industry debate has shifted from streaming adoption to monetization. Three debates are subscription pricing, ad-supported monetization and free-to-paid conversion, and Generative AI. GS views scaled DSPs as relative beneficiaries and sees a more balanced risk/reward for labels and rights holders.

market_movers.rationale: Shares -2% pre-market after a solid quarter with FY26 raised but 3Q GM a touch light and no color on FY27 CapEx.
Investor Day guidance of mid-single digit revenue growth in FY27-28 and 10-30bps annual margin expansion should mute the bear case. GS sees ACN as well positioned for enterprise AI work.
Raised PT ahead of F2Q on improving GTM productivity, large-deal execution, Logs strength and 20%+ consumption growth across DPS customers.
Two senior executives are leaving after the interim CEO's return. Management says there is no strategy change, but the CEO search adds uncertainty.
Q3 preview: GS revenue estimate of EUR4.964bn is modestly below guidance, and 2026 estimates are lowered on lower advertising revenue in 2H and FX.
Indicated -7% as Hynix fell 11% in Korea, with foreigners selling for 15 straight sessions.

sector_views.rationale: After SEMICON West, GS remains bullish on the group with an incrementally positive view on WFE growth for 2027 and 2028.
Memory stocks are under pressure from foreign selling and the China memory capacity narrative, while the memory crisis is hitting smartphone shipments.
